subject: Deployment mode: latency & qps thresholds — follow-up
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.com>
To: Kirsten Wu <kirsten@fastretail.com>, Alex Chen <alex@fastretail.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Jun 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Deployment mode: latency & qps thresholds — follow-up

Kirsten / Alex — thanks again for taking time today. Quick recap from our discovery so we have a shared set of constraints to qualify hosted vs dedicated: 

- Production traffic profile (your estimate): steady-state ~40–60 QPS with predictable daytime peaks up to ~200 QPS for short bursts (promo events, inventory sync).
- Typical prompt/response size: ~200–350 tokens per request (average ~250). Retrieval + generate pattern (embedding lookup + 2-stage prompt).
- Latency targets you called out: p95 < 120 ms (target), p99 tolerable up to ~400 ms but ideally < 300 ms for critical checkout flows.
- Model mix: planning to run a 13B tuned model for most requests, with smaller distilled models for simple classification routes.
- Security: not intending on on-prem for now; need encryption at rest/in-transit and audit logs; VPC option would be a 'nice-to-have' if procurement pushes for stronger network controls.

Notes on qualification: based on those numbers, Dedicated capacity is often what customers choose when p99 and peak burst behavior are strict and predictable because it gives consistent GPU pools and prewarmed caches. Hosted API can hit low p95s at low cost for spiky, unpredictable loads but may require routing/fallback policies for sustained high bursts.

Attachments: I attached a quick capacity sketch (capacity_estimate_v1.pdf) with three sizing options: 'Cost-optimized Hosted', 'Hybrid (hosted + fallback)', and 'Dedicated baseline + burst.'

Proposed next steps:
- Please share a short representative traffic dump or a CSV of QPS by 5–15 minute windows (we need 2–3 days if possible).
- Neha (cc) to run a technical sizing check once we have traces — recommend we schedule a 45-min technical deep dive.
- I can put together a preliminary cost/latency tradeoff (hosted vs dedicated) and a procurement checklist for Dedicated.

Can we aim for a technical deep-dive next week? Wed 15 Jun 10:00 PT or Thu 16 Jun 11:00 PT both look open on our side — pick what works for you and we’ll lock it.

Thanks,
Dylan Brooks
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
(attachment: capacity_estimate_v1.pdf)
From: Kirsten Wu <kirsten@fastretail.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Chen <alex@fastretail.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Jun 2027 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Deployment mode: latency & qps thresholds — follow-up

Thanks, Dylan — solid summary. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Our strict SLA bucket is checkout and personalization endpoints. For those, we'd prefer p95 < 100 ms and p99 ideally < 300 ms. Other endpoints (recommendations, analytics) can tolerate higher p99.
- The 200 QPS burst is realistic during promotions and load tests; bursts last ~10–25 minutes.
- Model: our engineering team will deploy a tuned 13B (gen+rerank) as primary, with a 7B fallback for non-critical queries. We expect ~70% of traffic to hit the 13B path initially.
- Security: we need SOC2 evidence and KMS integration; VPC would be evaluated but is not mandatory for initial deployment.

Requests from our procurement/infra side: can you provide an estimated lead time for Dedicated capacity (from SOW to capacity ready) and a ballpark delta in monthly cost vs hosted for our steady-state numbers? Also curious about burst autoscaling limits and how routing to Hosted fallback would work if Dedicated is saturated.

Happy to do Wed 15 Jun 10:00 PT for the deep-dive.

—Kirsten
Kirsten Wu
Head of AI, FastRetail
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.com>
To: Kirsten Wu <kirsten@fastretail.com>, Alex Chen <alex@fastretail.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, procurement@fastretail.com
Date: Fri, 11 Jun 2027 09:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Deployment mode: latency & qps thresholds — follow-up

Kirsten — great, Wed 15 Jun 10:00 PT is confirmed on our calendar (inv attached).

Addressing the procurement and capacity questions briefly and attaching a more detailed sizing workbook (dedicated_capacity_options.xlsx) and a preliminary ballpark (prelim_cost_ballpark.pdf):

- Lead time for Dedicated: typical timeline is 4–6 weeks from SOW to reserved capacity provisioned and smoke-tested (shorter if you accept an initial warmup window with burst routing to Hosted). We can compress to ~2–3 weeks for pilot with an accelerated ops path.
- Monthly cost delta: for steady-state 40–60 QPS on a 13B (with caching & batching) we estimate Dedicated baseline cost is ~2.5–3x lower per-unit inference cost vs fully hosted at sustained throughput because of reserved capacity economics; however Dedicated has higher fixed monthly commitment. See attached sheet for three commitment tiers.
- Burst autoscaling & fallback: our Dedicated product supports autoscale policies for short-term bursts up to a configured burst factor (we commonly set 1.5–2x). When autoscale limits are reached, traffic can be routed to a Hosted fallback model variant (configured by route) with graceful degradation (smaller model or higher latency). We will include an explicit fallback policy in the SOW.
- SLOs: we propose documenting p95/p99 SLOs per route; note that p99 variability often stems from cold KV cache and long-tail sequence lengths — prewarming and prefix caching will help tighten p99.

Requested from you ahead of the deep-dive:
1) representative 48–72 hour traffic timestamps + QPS buckets (CSV),
2) a sample of 50–100 prompts across your primary use cases (to calibrate token distribution),
3) list of routes that must hit the strict SLA (checkout / personalization).

DocuSign placeholder for a pilot SOW: https://docusign.example.com/FR-2027-042/pilot. If you want, we can include an optional clause for a 2-week Dedicated pilot with autoscale + hosted fallback and a procurement-friendly exit window.

Thanks — we'll bring Neha and Marissa to the deep dive to cover sizing and commercials.

Best,
Dylan
(attachments: dedicated_capacity_options.xlsx, prelim_cost_ballpark.pdf)
From: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
To: Kirsten Wu <kirsten@fastretail.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 11 Jun 2027 11:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Deployment mode: latency & qps thresholds — follow-up

Quick tech note before the deep-dive: 

- With a 13B quantized (int8) runtime on our recommended GPU class (A10G / equivalent), and with continuous batching tuned to your token distribution, we typically see p95 in the ~80–120 ms range for single-request generation at average prompt sizes (200–300 tokens). p99 depends heavily on sequence tail and cache hit rate — with warmed prefix caching (your repeated prompts / templates) p99 often falls under 300 ms for the class of workloads you described.
- For bursts, the critical pieces are: prewarmed KV cache, a warmed pool of workers (prewarmed GPUs), and aggressive request routing rules for short-lived overprovision. Autoscale can be set to 2x for short windows (10–30 mins) but sustained 2x for days is costly.
- Bring anything you can that represents worst-case long prompts and the ~10% longest requests — those are the ones that drive p99 outliers.

See you Wed 15 Jun 10:00 PT. I’ll prepare two sizing scenarios (conservative and aggressive) and a short checklist for procurement items we’ll need to speed a Dedicated pilot.

—Neha
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
